title: How Migrating Birds Navigate Without A Map

media.title: File:PSM V09 D158 Crane throat structure.jpg

script: How do migrating birds cross entire continents without a map? The secret lies in a built-in GPS that puts our best technology to shame. First, they read the position of the sun by day and map the constellations by night, using the North Star as their compass. But that is not all. During cloudy days, birds actually see the Earth’s invisible magnetic field through specialized proteins in their eyes. This quantum compass allows them to feel magnetic pulls and steer across thousands of miles to the exact same tree they left behind last year. Nature's greatest navigators are truly out of this world.
